channel.title: Ayatullah Syed Sibtain Abbas Rizvi — Islamic Jurisprudence & Q&A
channel.description: Official answered questions and legal rulings on Islamic jurisprudence (Fiqh) by Ayatullah Syed Sibtain Abbas Rizvi for the followers of Ahlulbayt (a.s.).

item.title: Is it permissible to combine Dhuhr and Asr prayers without travel or rain?
item.description: According to the jurisprudence of the Ahlulbayt (a.s.), it is permissible in all circumstances to combine Dhuhr with Asr prayers, and Maghrib with Isha prayers, both when traveling and when residing at home. However, offering each prayer at its designated prime (fadhilah) time is superior and more meritorious.

item.title: What is the ruling if a person doubts whether they prayed 3 or 4 rak'ats in Isha prayer?
item.description: If the doubt arises after completing the second prostration (sajdah) of the fourth rak'ah, the person assumes they have prayed four rak'ats, finishes the prayer with taslim, and immediately performs one rak'ah of Salaat al-Ihtiyat (prayer of precaution) standing, or two rak'ats sitting.

item.title: Does using an asthma inhaler invalidate the fast during the Holy Month of Ramadan?
item.description: If the medicinal spray entering the throat reaches only the respiratory tract and lungs to relieve breathing, and does not enter the stomach as liquid or food nourishment, the fast remains valid.

item.title: What is the ruling on traveling during the month of Ramadan before and after noon (Zawal)?
item.description: If a fasting person embarks on a journey after the time of Zawal (solar noon), their fast for that day remains valid and they must continue fasting until Maghrib. If they travel before Zawal and cross the boundaries of Tarakh-khus, they break their fast and must make up (qadha) that day later.

item.title: Does having a medical bandage or plaster prevent performing normal Wudhu?
item.description: If removing the bandage causes significant harm, acute pain, or difficulty, one should perform Wudhu al-Jabirah. The exposed parts are washed normally, and a wet hand is gently wiped over the clean bandage or covering.
